courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Elementary Greek I
courses.description: Introduces ancient Greek (both classical and koine), including the reading of simple prose. Same as REL 111.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Elementary Greek II
courses.description: Continuation of GRK 101. Grammar and reading in classical and koine Greek. Same as REL 112.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Classical & Koine Greek I
courses.description: Readings in classical Greek prose, and narrative and epistolary New Testament texts. Same as REL 200.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Classical & Koine Greek II
courses.description: Continuation of GRK 201. Further readings in classical Greek prose, and narrative and epistolary New Testament texts. Same as REL 204.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Survey of Greek Literature
courses.description: Advanced level readings in Ancient Greek literature. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Greek Prose Composition
courses.description: Practice in the writing of Greek prose. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Readings in Greek Literature
courses.description: Readings in authors or special topics chosen by the instructor from the entire extant literature in Greek. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms, if topics vary.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Thesis and honors. Open to candidates for distinction in Greek. 2 to 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing and consent of Classics Honors Program.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Independent Reading
courses.description: 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. 1 to 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 undergraduate hours or 12 graduate hours.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Advanced Composition
courses.description: Practice in writing continuous Greek prose, with special attention to stylistic problems.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Proseminar
courses.description: Alternating poetry and prose, concentrates on a major author from one of the following areas: epic, history, lyric poetry, oratory, drama, or philosophy. Areas normally follow this sequence in successive years. May be repeated to a maximum of 20 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Special Disciplines
courses.description: Variable content course concentrating on an area such as comparative grammar, epigraphy, metrics, palaeography, or papyrology. Same as LAT 531. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Greek Seminar
courses.description: Research on special problems of Greek literature; required of all majors in classical philology. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Intro to Classical Studies
courses.description: Introductory survey for graduate students in classics; prepares students for work at the graduate level and surveys basic bibliography and methodology. Same as LAT 595.

courses.subject: GRK
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Guidance in writing theses for advanced degrees. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms.
